prompt: We're staring at a Redis Cluster read path that's about to ship a "fix" I don't trust. The cluster has a handful of masters (hash slots sharded across them), each with one replica, and it backs a read-heavy service — cached profile/catalog lookups that can tolerate a bit of staleness, plus a steady stream of writes. The masters are pegged on CPU and network while the replicas sit almost idle. Below is the client setup and the code path that talks to the cluster, plus a comment describing the team's already-drafted PR to "just add more replicas" to relieve the saturation. Walk through what's actually wrong here, then tell me how you'd change this code to fix it — and tell the team whether their replica-adding plan will work.
